What Critical Mass is

Critical Mass started in San Francisco on Friday, September 25, 1992, as a ride called the Commute Clot; it had its name by the second one. It has no leader, no membership and no set route: whoever is at the front picks the turns, or the group does. Most cities ride on the last Friday of the month, after work.

The name comes from George Bliss in Ted White’s film “Return of the Scorcher”: at crossings in China, he said, riders and drivers built up until there were enough of them, a critical mass, and then went through together. In 2022 Chris Carlsson told KQED it rides in more than 400 cities.

Sources: Critical Mass (cycling), Wikipedia; KQED, Oct 1, 2022. Read Oct 26, 2026.

About these 36 rides

The earliest start is Critical Mass Wien at 5:00 pm; the latest is Massa Crítica Barcelona at 8:00 pm. All of them start at 5 pm or later, after work. The group waits for everyone on 14 of them (no-drop), and beginners are welcome on 4. There are 2 rides made for families. All 36 are social rides. Each one was checked at its source between Sep 15 and Oct 26, 2026.
